facts: Inverting an interval moves its lower note up an octave (or its upper note down an octave).
An interval and its inversion add up to nine: a third becomes a sixth, a second a seventh, a fourth a fifth.
Inversion swaps major and minor, swaps augmented and diminished, and keeps perfect perfect.
C up to E is a major third, so E up to C is a minor sixth.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: C3 (string 5 fret 3) up to E3 (string 4 fret 2), then E3 up to C4 (string 3 fret 5); audio of both.

exercises.idea: What is the inversion of a major second? (minor seventh)
Match each interval to its inversion: M3 / m6, P4 / P5, m2 / M7, A4 / d5.
A perfect fifth inverts to a perfect _ (fourth).

lessons.title: Interval shapes on neighbouring strings
lessons.teaches: On neighbouring strings (except G and B) the same fret is a fourth, and each fret either side changes the interval by a half step.
facts: On neighbouring strings (not the G-B pair), the same fret is a perfect fourth.
On the next thinner string, one fret higher is a tritone and two frets higher a perfect fifth.
On the next thinner string, one fret lower is a major third and two frets lower a minor third.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: root A on string 6 fret 5 with string 5 frets 3 (C, m3), 4 (C#, M3), 5 (D, P4), 6 (D#, A4) and 7 (E, P5) labelled.

exercises.idea: From G on string 6 fret 3, tap the perfect fifth on string 5 (fret 5, D).
Two dots: string 5 fret 7 and string 4 fret 6. Name the interval (major third).
From D on string 5 fret 5, tap the minor third on string 4 (fret 3, F).

lessons.title: Sixths, sevenths and octaves across a string
lessons.teaches: With one string in between (not crossing G-B), two frets higher is an octave and each fret lower shrinks the interval by a half step.
facts: With one string between (strings 6 to 4, or 5 to 3), two frets higher is an octave.
One fret higher is a major seventh, the same fret a minor seventh.
One fret lower is a major sixth and two frets lower a minor sixth.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: root G on string 6 fret 3 with string 4 frets 1 (Eb, m6), 2 (E, M6), 3 (F, m7), 4 (F#, M7) and 5 (G, P8) labelled.

exercises.idea: From C on string 5 fret 3, tap the minor seventh on string 3 (fret 3, Bb).
Two dots: string 6 fret 5 and string 4 fret 4. Name the interval (major sixth).
From string 6 to string 4, one fret higher is an octave (false).

lessons.title: The B-string shift
lessons.teaches: Any interval shape that crosses from string 3 to string 2 needs one extra fret on string 2.
facts: A shape that crosses from string 3 to string 2 moves one fret higher on string 2 than on other string pairs.
The same fret on strings 3 and 2 is a major third, not a perfect fourth.
From A on string 3 fret 2, the perfect fourth is D on string 2 fret 3 and the perfect fifth E on string 2 fret 5.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: the P4 and P5 shapes drawn on strings 5-4 and again on strings 3-2, with the one-fret shift highlighted.

exercises.idea: From C on string 3 fret 5, tap the perfect fifth on string 2 (fret 8, G).
Strings 3 and 2 at the same fret make which interval? (major third)
From G on string 4 fret 5, tap the octave on string 2 (fret 8).

lessons.title: Ninths, elevenths and thirteenths
lessons.teaches: Intervals larger than an octave are compound intervals, named by adding 7 to the simple interval's number.
facts: An interval larger than an octave is a compound interval.
Adding an octave adds 7 to the number: a ninth is a second plus an octave, an eleventh a fourth plus an octave, a thirteenth a sixth plus an octave.
A major ninth is 14 half steps, a perfect eleventh 17 and a major thirteenth 21.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: C on string 5 fret 3 with D on string 2 fret 3 (M9), F on string 1 fret 1 (P11) and A on string 1 fret 5 (M13).

exercises.idea: A ninth is an octave plus which interval? (a second)
Match: M9 / 14, P11 / 17, M13 / 21 half steps.
An eleventh is a _ plus an octave (fourth).

lessons.title: Stable and tense
lessons.teaches: Consonant intervals sound stable and dissonant ones sound tense and want to move.
facts: Consonant intervals sound stable; dissonant intervals sound tense and seem to want to move.
Unisons, octaves and perfect fifths are perfect consonances; thirds and sixths are imperfect consonances.
Seconds, sevenths and the tritone are dissonant.
In classical harmony a perfect fourth above the bass is treated as a dissonance.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Audio: harmonic intervals from A2 (open string 5): P8, P5, M3, M6, then m2, M7 and the tritone. Figure: each as two dots on the neck.

exercises.idea: Two notes together: consonant or dissonant?
Which is an imperfect consonance: a perfect fifth, a major sixth or a minor second? (major sixth)
Hear two notes together and name the interval (P5, M3, m7, P8).

units.checkpoint: Quality rules (perfect versus major and minor; augmented and diminished); spelling by letter count (C-D# versus C-Eb); inversions that add to nine with qualities swapped; the adjacent-string shapes from m3 to P5 and the one-string-between shapes from m6 to P8; the extra fret when a shape crosses from string 3 to string 2; ninths, elevenths and thirteenths and their sizes; consonance and dissonance by ear.

units.title: Key signatures and the circle of fifths
units.summary: How key signatures work, the order of sharps and flats, naming keys from signatures, and the circle of fifths.
units.whyItMatters: The circle tells you at a glance which keys and chords are close relatives, which is how songs and modulations are built.

lessons.title: What a key signature is
lessons.teaches: A key signature lists the sharps or flats of the key once at the start of each staff line, and they apply to every note with that letter.
facts: A key signature is the group of sharps or flats written at the start of every staff line.
A sharp or flat in the key signature applies to every note with that letter, in every octave, unless cancelled.
C major has no sharps or flats.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: staff with the G major signature (F# on the top line) and a melody with Fs in two octaves, each played as F# (string 1 fret 2 and string 4 fret 4); audio.

exercises.idea: With one sharp (F#) in the signature, name the note on the bottom space (F#).
A sharp in the key signature only affects notes on that exact line (false).
How many sharps or flats does C major have? (none)

lessons.title: The sharp keys
lessons.teaches: Each sharp key starts a perfect fifth above the last and adds one sharp, in the fixed order F C G D A E B.
facts: Each new sharp key starts a perfect fifth above the last: C, G, D, A, E, B, F#, C#.
G major has 1 sharp, D 2, A 3, E 4, B 5, F# 6 and C# 7.
Sharps are written in the order F C G D A E B.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: staff showing the signatures of G, D, A and E major; on the neck, the tonics G, D, A and E climbing in fifths (string 6 fret 3, string 5 fret 5, string 4 fret 7, string 3 fret 9).

exercises.idea: How many sharps does E major have? (4)
Put the sharps in signature order: C#, F#, D#, G# (F#, C#, G#, D#).
Sharp keys: C, G, D, _, E, _ (A, B).

lessons.title: Naming a sharp key
lessons.teaches: In a sharp signature the last sharp is degree 7 of the major key, so the key is a half step above it.
facts: In a sharp key signature the last sharp is degree 7 of the major key; the key is a half step above it.
Three sharps (F# C# G#): G# plus a half step gives A major.
A memory sentence for the order of sharps: Father Charles Goes Down And Ends Battle.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: staff with the four-sharp signature, the last sharp (D#) circled and an arrow up a half step to E; fretboard showing D# to E on string 5 (frets 6 to 7).

exercises.idea: A signature has two sharps. Which major key? (D)
Type the major key with five sharps (B).
With four sharps the key is a half step above D#, so E major (true).

lessons.title: The flat keys
lessons.teaches: Each flat key starts a perfect fifth below the last and adds one flat, in the order B E A D G C F.
facts: Each new flat key starts a perfect fifth below the last: C, F, Bb, Eb, Ab, Db, Gb, Cb.
Flats are written in the order B E A D G C F, the order of sharps reversed.
F major has 1 flat, Bb 2, Eb 3, Ab 4, Db 5, Gb 6 and Cb 7.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: staff with the signatures of F, Bb, Eb and Ab major; on the neck, their tonics at fret 1 of strings 6, 5, 4 and 3 (F, Bb, Eb, Ab), each a fourth higher than the last, which gives the same note name as a fifth lower.

exercises.idea: How many flats does Eb major have? (3)
Put these flats in signature order: Ab, Bb, Db, Eb (Bb, Eb, Ab, Db).
Flat keys: F, Bb, _, Ab, _ (Eb, Db).

lessons.title: Naming a flat key
lessons.teaches: With two or more flats, the second-to-last flat names the major key; one flat is F major.
facts: With two or more flats, the second-to-last flat names the major key: Bb Eb Ab gives Eb major.
One flat (Bb) is F major.
Every flat major key except F has a flat in its name.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: staff with the three-flat signature, the second-to-last flat (Eb) circled, and the Eb major tonic on the neck at string 5 fret 6.

exercises.idea: Four flats (Bb Eb Ab Db): which major key? (Ab)
Type the major key with two flats (Bb).
One flat is Bb major (false).

lessons.title: The circle of fifths
lessons.teaches: The circle of fifths puts the twelve major keys around a clock in rising fifths, with sharps added clockwise and flats anticlockwise.
facts: The circle of fifths places the major keys clockwise in rising perfect fifths: C G D A E B F#(Gb) Db Ab Eb Bb F.
Going clockwise adds a sharp or removes a flat; going anticlockwise adds a flat or removes a sharp.
At the bottom of the circle three pairs of keys sound the same: B and Cb, F# and Gb, C# and Db.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: the circle of fifths with signature counts; on the neck, fifths climb by the P5 shape (string 6 fret 3 G to string 5 fret 5 D to string 4 fret 7 A).

exercises.idea: Put these keys in circle order clockwise from C: A, G, E, D (G, D, A, E).
Which key is clockwise from Eb? (Bb)
F# major and Gb major sound the same (true).

lessons.title: Neighbours on the circle
lessons.teaches: Keys next to each other on the circle differ by one note, and the I, IV and V chords are the home key and its two neighbours.
facts: Neighbouring keys on the circle differ by only one note: C major and G major differ only by F and F#.
The key one step clockwise is the dominant key (built on degree 5); one step anticlockwise is the subdominant key (built on degree 4).
The I, IV and V chords of a key sit together on the circle: in C, the chords F, C and G.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: the circle with C, its clockwise neighbour G and its anticlockwise neighbour F highlighted; chord boxes of C, F (small F, xx3211) and G.

exercises.idea: Which key differs from D major by just one note: A major or Bb major? (A major)
What is the subdominant key of G major? (C major)
Match each key to its I-IV-V: C / C F G, G / G C D, D / D G A.
A short melody in C is played, then again with every F raised to F#: which version is in G major?

units.checkpoint: What a key signature applies to; the order of sharps (F C G D A E B) and flats (B E A D G C F); naming a major key from its signature (last sharp plus a half step; second-to-last flat; one flat is F); the number of sharps or flats in each major key; the circle clockwise in fifths, its three enharmonic pairs, neighbours that differ by one note; I, IV and V as circle neighbours.

units.title: The minor scales
units.summary: Natural, harmonic and melodic minor, relative and parallel keys, minor key signatures, and minor on the neck.
units.whyItMatters: Minor keys are half of all music, and knowing the three minors explains why minor songs so often use a major V chord.

lessons.title: The natural minor scale
lessons.teaches: Natural minor follows W H W W H W W, which is the major scale with a flat 3rd, 6th and 7th.
facts: The natural minor scale follows the step pattern W H W W H W W.
Compared with the major scale on the same tonic, natural minor has a flat 3rd, 6th and 7th: 1 2 b3 4 5 b6 b7.
A natural minor is A B C D E F G: all natural notes, starting on A.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: A natural minor along string 5 (frets 0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12) with W and H marked; audio.

exercises.idea: Natural minor step pattern: W H W W _ W W (H).
Which degrees are flattened in natural minor compared with major? (3, 6 and 7)
Type degree b6 of E natural minor (C).

lessons.title: The relative minor
lessons.teaches: Every major key has a relative minor with the same notes, whose tonic is degree 6 of the major scale.
facts: Every major key has a relative minor that uses the same notes and the same key signature.
The relative minor's tonic is degree 6 of the major scale, a minor third (three half steps) below the major tonic.
C major and A minor are relatives; so are G major and E minor, and F major and D minor.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: C major (string 5 fret 3) and A minor (string 6 fret 5) on the neck, with the shared notes lit in both colours.

exercises.idea: What is the relative minor of D major? (B minor)
Type the relative major of F# minor (A).
From C on string 5 fret 3, tap the relative minor tonic three frets lower (fret 0, A).

lessons.title: The parallel minor
lessons.teaches: Parallel major and minor share a tonic but not their notes; relative keys share notes but not a tonic.
facts: Parallel major and minor keys share the same tonic: C major and C minor.
C natural minor is C D Eb F G Ab Bb, with three flats in its key signature.
Relative keys share notes; parallel keys share a tonic.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: C major and C natural minor both from string 5 fret 3 in one-octave shapes, with Eb, Ab and Bb highlighted; audio of both.

exercises.idea: What is the parallel minor of G major? (G minor)
Match: C major and A minor / relative; C major and C minor / parallel.
Same tonic, two scales: which is minor?

lessons.title: Minor key signatures
lessons.teaches: A minor key uses the key signature of its relative major, so each signature belongs to one major and one minor key.
facts: A minor key uses the same key signature as its relative major.
To find the minor key of a signature, find the major key and go down a minor third: one sharp is G major or E minor.
Which of the two keys a piece is in is shown by the chord and note it treats as home.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: staff with one sharp labelled "G major or E minor", two flats labelled "Bb major or G minor"; on the neck, the two one-sharp tonics three frets apart on string 6 (E open, G at fret 3); audio of a phrase ending on G and one ending on E.

exercises.idea: Which minor key has two sharps? (B minor)
Three flats: which minor key? (C minor)
A one-sharp melody: does it settle on G (major) or on E (minor)?

lessons.title: Harmonic minor
lessons.teaches: Harmonic minor raises the 7th of natural minor, giving a leading tone and a major V chord.
facts: Harmonic minor is natural minor with a raised 7th: 1 2 b3 4 5 b6 7.
A harmonic minor is A B C D E F G#.
The raised 7th is a leading tone a half step below the tonic, and it turns the minor v chord into a major V (E instead of Em in A minor).
The step from b6 to 7 (F to G# in A) is an augmented second, three half steps, which gives harmonic minor its distinctive sound.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: A harmonic minor along string 5 (frets 0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 11, 12) with the F to G# gap highlighted; audio; chord boxes of Em (022000) and E (022100).

exercises.idea: Type the raised 7th of D harmonic minor (C#).
Natural minor or harmonic minor?
How many half steps are between degrees b6 and 7 of harmonic minor? (3)

lessons.title: Melodic minor
lessons.teaches: Melodic minor raises both the 6th and the 7th of natural minor, smoothing out the augmented second.
facts: Melodic minor raises the 6th and 7th of natural minor: 1 2 b3 4 5 6 7.
A melodic minor is A B C D E F# G#.
In classical music the raised form is used going up and natural minor coming down; in jazz the raised form is used both ways.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: A melodic minor along string 5 (frets 0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 12) and the classical descending form (natural minor); audio.

exercises.idea: A melodic minor: A B C D E _ _ A (F#, G#).
Melodic minor differs from the major scale on the same tonic by one note. Which degree? (the 3rd)
Which minor scale did you hear: natural, harmonic or melodic?

lessons.title: A minor in fifth position
lessons.teaches: A natural minor in fifth position is box 1 of A minor pentatonic with two notes added: B and F.
facts: A natural minor is A minor pentatonic plus B (degree 2) and F (degree b6).
Around box 1 at fret 5, the added B notes are at string 6 fret 7, string 3 fret 4 and string 1 fret 7.
The added F notes are at string 5 fret 8 and string 2 fret 6.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Fifth position means the first finger at fret 5, one finger per fret, with a stretch back to fret 4 for the B on string 3. Figure: box 1 of A minor pentatonic in plain dots with the added B and F notes in a second colour, frets 4 to 8; tab ascending; audio.

exercises.idea: Tap every F in fifth position (string 5 fret 8, string 2 fret 6).
Play A natural minor in fifth position from string 6 fret 5 up to string 1 fret 8.
Which two notes turn A minor pentatonic into A natural minor? (B and F)

units.checkpoint: Natural minor as W H W W H W W and 1 2 b3 4 5 b6 b7; the relative minor (degree 6, a minor third below) versus the parallel minor (same tonic); minor key signatures; harmonic minor (raised 7th, augmented second) and melodic minor (raised 6th and 7th, the classical up-and-down use); hearing the three minors; A natural minor in fifth position as the pentatonic plus B and F.

units.title: Rhythm: triplets, swing and syncopation
units.summary: Triplets, swing and shuffle feel, syncopation and anticipations, sixteenth-note grooves, and tempo words.
units.whyItMatters: These rhythms are what make blues, funk, rock and pop guitar parts feel alive instead of stiff.

lessons.title: Triplets
lessons.teaches: A triplet fits three notes into the time normally taken by two of the same kind.
facts: A triplet fits three notes into the time normally taken by two of the same kind.
Three eighth-note triplets last one quarter-note beat.
Triplets are marked with a 3 over the group and can be counted "1-trip-let 2-trip-let".
lessons.onTheGuitar: Pick open string 1 in eighth notes, then in eighth-note triplets, at 70 BPM. Figure: rhythm line of one beat of eighths beside one beat of triplets; audio.

exercises.idea: Tap one bar: two beats of eighth-note triplets, then two quarter notes, at 70 BPM.
Did you hear eighth notes or triplets?
How many eighth-note triplets fill one quarter-note beat? (3)

lessons.title: Swing feel
lessons.teaches: In swing, pairs of eighth notes are played long-short, close to the first and last notes of a triplet.
facts: In swing, pairs of eighth notes are played long-short instead of evenly.
A swung eighth-note pair is close to a triplet quarter note followed by a triplet eighth note: a 2:1 ratio.
Swing is usually written as ordinary eighth notes with "Swing" (or a swing sign) at the top of the music.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Pick a two-note phrase on string 2 (frets 1 and 3) in straight eighths, then swung, at 90 BPM. Figure: rhythm line of eighths with the swing sign and the triplet picture it means; audio of both.

exercises.idea: Straight or swung eighth notes?
Tap one bar of swung eighth notes at 90 BPM.
In swing, pairs of eighth notes are played evenly (false).

lessons.title: The shuffle
lessons.teaches: A shuffle is a swung groove for a whole song, and guitarists play it with a two-string root-fifth, root-sixth pattern.
facts: A shuffle is a swung rhythm used as the groove of a whole song, as in blues and boogie.
The classic guitar shuffle in A alternates open string 5 with string 4 at fret 2 (A5) and at fret 4 (the 6th, F#).
Shuffles are sometimes written in 12/8 so that the triplet feel is shown exactly.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: tab of the A shuffle: open string 5 with string 4 frets 2, 2, 4, 4 (swung eighths), then the same on strings 4-3 for D and 6-5 for E; audio at 100 BPM.

exercises.idea: Play one bar of the A shuffle: string 5 open with string 4 at frets 2, 2, 4, 4, swung.
Is this groove a shuffle or straight eighths?
Tap the two notes of the shuffle's "6" shape on strings 6 and 5 for E (open string 6, string 5 fret 4).

lessons.title: Syncopation
lessons.teaches: Syncopation puts accents and note starts where the beat does not lead you to expect them, usually on off-beats.
facts: Syncopation means stressing or starting notes off the beat, where the listener does not expect them.
An anticipation is a chord or note that arrives early, often by an eighth note on the "&" before a beat, and is usually tied over.
A common syncopated strum ties the "&" of 2 over beat 3, so beat 3 is not struck.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Strum G (320003) with the pattern down (1), down-up (2 &), tie over 3, up (& of 3), down-up (4 &). Figure: rhythm line with the tie and counts; audio.

exercises.idea: Tap: 1, 2, & (tied over 3), & of 3, 4, & of 4.
Which bar is syncopated?
In strummed pop and rock, how early does an anticipation most often arrive? (an eighth note, on the "&" before the beat)

lessons.title: Sixteenth-note grooves
lessons.teaches: Sixteenth-note figures are named by where they fall in "1 e & a", and the "e" and "a" are the most off-beat spots.
facts: In sixteenth-note rhythms the "e" and the "a" are the most off-beat positions.
An eighth note then two sixteenths in one beat is counted "1 & a"; two sixteenths then an eighth is "1 e &".
Sixteenth, eighth, sixteenth in one beat is counted "1 e a": the middle note starts on the "e".
Funk rhythm guitar keeps the hand moving in sixteenths and strikes only some of them.
A dotted eighth then a sixteenth fills one beat, counted "1 (e &) a": the sixteenth falls on the "a".
lessons.onTheGuitar: Strum the muted strings with the hand moving in sixteenths at 70 BPM, striking only the notes of each figure; then play the same figures on Em7 (022030). Figure: rhythm line of the figures with counts and arrows; audio.

exercises.idea: Tap one beat each of "1 & a", "1 e &" and "1 e a", then a quarter note.
Sixteenth, eighth, sixteenth is counted 1 e _ (a).
Hear one beat and choose its figure.

lessons.title: Tempo words
lessons.teaches: Italian words in music set the tempo and tell you when to speed up or slow down.
facts: Adagio means slow, Andante at a walking pace, Moderato moderate, Allegro fast and bright, Presto very fast.
Ritardando (rit.) means gradually slow down; accelerando (accel.) means gradually speed up.
A tempo means go back to the original speed.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: a short original line on strings 1 and 2 (frets 0 to 3) on the staff, marked Andante, with rit. at the end and a tempo afterwards; metronome showing a typical Andante (about 76 to 108 BPM).

exercises.idea: Match: Adagio / slow, Andante / walking pace, Allegro / fast and bright, Presto / very fast.
Did the music slow down (rit.) or speed up (accel.)?
What does "a tempo" mean? (return to the original speed)

units.checkpoint: Triplets as three in the time of two and how to count them; swing as long-short pairs close to a 2:1 triplet feel; the shuffle; syncopation and anticipations; the sixteenth-note figures 1 & a, 1 e &, 1 e a and the dotted eighth plus sixteenth; tempo words and rit., accel. and a tempo.

units.title: Triads and inversions
units.summary: The four kinds of triad, inversions and slash names, and compact triad shapes across the neck.
units.whyItMatters: Small triad shapes let you play any chord high on the neck, which is how good rhythm guitarists fit around a band.

lessons.title: Major, minor, diminished, augmented
lessons.teaches: Stacking two thirds gives four kinds of triad: major, minor, diminished and augmented.
facts: Major is a major third plus a minor third, minor a minor plus a major, diminished two minor thirds, augmented two major thirds.
Formulas: major 1 3 5, minor 1 b3 5, diminished 1 b3 b5, augmented 1 3 #5.
C diminished is C Eb Gb; C augmented is C E G#.
Diminished is written dim or °; augmented is written aug or +.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: on strings 4-3-2, C (10-9-8), Cm (10-8-8), Cdim (10-8-7) and Caug (10-9-9), each dot labelled with its degree; audio of all four.

exercises.idea: Major, minor, diminished or augmented?
C augmented: C E _ (G#).
Which triad is two minor thirds stacked? (diminished)

lessons.title: Root position and inversions
lessons.teaches: A triad's inversion is named by its lowest note: root, third (first inversion) or fifth (second inversion).
facts: A triad is in root position when the root is the lowest note.
It is in first inversion when the third is lowest and in second inversion when the fifth is lowest.
Slash chords can name inversions: C/E is C major with E in the bass (first inversion); C/G is second inversion.
Open C (x32010) is in root position; adding open string 6 (032010) makes it C/E.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: chord boxes of C (x32010), C/E (032010) and C/G (332010), bass notes labelled; audio.

exercises.idea: Place C/G: open C with string 6 fret 3 added (332010).
Which inversion is G/B? (first inversion)
Is the bass note the root or not?

lessons.title: Major triads on the top three strings
lessons.teaches: On strings 3, 2 and 1 each major triad has three shapes, one per inversion, that repeat up the neck in a fixed order.
facts: On strings 3, 2 and 1 every major triad has three shapes, one for each inversion.
G major on strings 3-2-1: first inversion at frets 4-3-3, second inversion at 7-8-7, root position at 12-12-10.
Up the neck the shapes cycle first inversion, second inversion, root position, then repeat twelve frets higher.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: fretboard frets 2 to 16 showing the three G major shapes on strings 3-2-1 with the root, third and fifth labelled; audio.

exercises.idea: Place G major in second inversion on strings 3-2-1 (frets 7, 8, 7).
Tap the three notes of A major in first inversion on strings 3-2-1 (frets 6, 5, 5).
In the 7-8-7 G shape, which string has the root? (string 2)

lessons.title: Minor triads on the top three strings
lessons.teaches: Each minor triad shape on strings 3-2-1 is the major shape with its third lowered one fret.
facts: Each minor triad shape is the matching major shape with the third lowered by one fret.
G minor on strings 3-2-1: first inversion 3-3-3, second inversion 7-8-6, root position 12-11-10.
Knowing where the third is in each shape lets you switch between major and minor anywhere on the neck.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: the G major and G minor shapes on strings 3-2-1 side by side, the moving third highlighted; audio pairs.

exercises.idea: Place G minor in root position on strings 3-2-1 (frets 12, 11, 10).
In the G major shape 7-8-7, tap the note you lower to make G minor (string 1, fret 7).
Major or minor triad?

lessons.title: Triads on strings 4, 3 and 2
lessons.teaches: On strings 4-3-2 the triad shapes differ from those on 3-2-1 because of the B string, but the method is the same.
facts: On strings 4-3-2 the triad shapes differ from those on strings 3-2-1, because string 2 is the B string.
F major on strings 4-3-2: root position 3-2-1, first inversion 7-5-6, second inversion 10-10-10.
The small F chord (xx3211) is the root-position shape with F added on string 1.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: fretboard frets 1 to 12 with the three F major shapes on strings 4-3-2, degrees labelled; audio.

exercises.idea: Place F major in second inversion on strings 4-3-2 (frets 10, 10, 10).
Strings 4-3-2 at frets 7-5-6: which chord and inversion is it? (F, first inversion)
Triad shapes on strings 4-3-2 are the same as on strings 3-2-1 (false).

lessons.title: The chords of a key on three strings
lessons.teaches: Moving triads up the scale on one string set plays the chords of the key in order.
facts: Moving a triad up the scale on one string set plays the diatonic chords in order.
Root-position triads of C major on strings 3-2-1: C 5-5-3, Dm 7-6-5, Em 9-8-7, F 10-10-8, G 12-12-10, Am 14-13-12.
The shape changes from chord to chord because major, minor and diminished triads have different shapes.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: fretboard frets 3 to 16 with the C major triads on strings 3-2-1 labelled with roman numerals; audio climbing I to vii° and back.

exercises.idea: Play the C major triads up strings 3-2-1 from C (5-5-3) to Am (14-13-12).
Place Em in root position on strings 3-2-1 (frets 9, 8, 7).
Which C major chord is played at 10-10-8 on strings 3-2-1? (F)

units.checkpoint: The four triad types as stacked thirds and their formulas; root position, first and second inversion and their slash names; the three major and minor shapes on strings 3-2-1 and their order up the neck; the F major shapes on strings 4-3-2; the chords of a key as triads on one string set.

units.title: CAGED: five shapes, one neck
units.summary: How the open C, A, G, E and D shapes become barre chords, link up to cover the whole neck, and frame the five positions of the major scale.
units.whyItMatters: CAGED turns five chords you already know into a map of the entire fretboard.

lessons.title: Five shapes: C, A, G, E, D
lessons.teaches: The open C, A, G, E and D chords are five movable shapes that, linked together, cover the neck.
facts: The open major chords C, A, G, E and D are the five shapes of the CAGED system.
Each shape can be moved up the neck if a finger or a barre replaces its open strings.
The word CAGED gives the order in which the shapes follow each other up the neck.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: chord boxes of C (x32010), A (x02220), G (320003), E (022100) and D (xx0232), each root dot highlighted.

exercises.idea: Place open D (xx0232); its lowest root is open string 4.
Put the shapes in CAGED order: E, C, D, A, G (C, A, G, E, D).
On which string is the lowest root of the A shape? (string 5)

lessons.title: The barre replaces the nut
lessons.teaches: A barre is one finger pressing several strings at one fret, doing the job of the nut in a moved open shape.
facts: A barre is one finger, usually the first, pressing several strings at the same fret.
In a moved open shape, the barre does the job of the nut.
Press with the bony side of the first finger close behind the fret, thumb behind the neck, and check each string rings.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: open E (022100) and the same shape at fret 1 with a barre (133211, F), the barre drawn as a curved bar; tab; audio of each string picked to check it rings.

exercises.idea: Place F as an E-shape barre at fret 1 (133211).
Play F (133211), then pick each string to check it rings.
In a moved open shape the barre does the job of the nut (true).

lessons.title: E-shape barre chords
lessons.teaches: The E shape moved up with a barre gives a major or minor chord named after its root on string 6.
facts: The E-shape barre chord is the open E shape moved up, with a first-finger barre across all six strings.
Its root is the barred note on string 6: at fret 1 it is F (133211), at fret 3 G (355433), at fret 5 A (577655).
Lifting the finger from string 3 gives the E-minor shape: F minor is 133111.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: chord boxes of F (133211), G (355433) and Fm (133111) with the string 6 root labelled; neck with string 6 note names.

exercises.idea: Build A major as an E-shape barre (577655).
An E-shape barre at fret 8 is which chord? (C)
Build G minor as an E-minor-shape barre (355333).
An E-shape barre chord is played: major or minor?

lessons.title: A-shape barre chords
lessons.teaches: The A shape moved up with a barre gives a major or minor chord named after its root on string 5.
facts: The A-shape barre chord is the open A shape moved up, with a barre on strings 5 to 1.
Its root is the barred note on string 5: at fret 1 it is Bb (x13331), at fret 2 B (x24442), at fret 3 C (x35553).
The A-minor shape at fret 2 is B minor (x24432).
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: chord boxes of Bb (x13331), C (x35553) and Bm (x24432) with the string 5 root labelled.

exercises.idea: Build D major as an A-shape barre (x57775).
An A-minor-shape barre at fret 7 is which chord? (Em)
Build C minor as an A-minor-shape barre (x35543).

lessons.title: C-A-G-E-D up the neck
lessons.teaches: For any major chord, the five shapes follow each other up the neck in the order C-A-G-E-D and then repeat.
facts: For any major chord the five shapes follow each other up the neck in the order C-A-G-E-D, then repeat.
C major: C shape in open position, A shape barred at fret 3, G shape around frets 5 to 8, E shape barred at fret 8, D shape with its root on string 4 fret 10.
Neighbouring shapes share notes: the top edge of one shape is the bottom edge of the next.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: fretboard frets 0 to 15 with the five C major shapes outlined in turn and the shared notes ringed; audio of C played in each shape.

exercises.idea: Put the C major shapes in order from the nut: E shape, C shape, D shape, A shape, G shape (C, A, G, E, D).
Tap the C roots of the A shape at fret 3 (string 5 fret 3, string 3 fret 5).
Which shape comes after the G shape going up? (E)

lessons.title: One chord in five places
lessons.teaches: Any major chord can be found in all five shapes by locating its roots on strings 6, 5 and 4.
facts: To find a chord in all five shapes, find its roots on strings 6, 5 and 4 and build each shape around them.
G major up the neck: G shape (open), E shape (fret 3), D shape (around fret 5), C shape (around fret 7), A shape (fret 10), then the G shape again from fret 12.
The same order works for minor chords using the minor versions of the shapes.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: fretboard frets 0 to 15 with the five G major shapes outlined and the G roots on strings 6, 5 and 4 highlighted.

exercises.idea: Tap the G roots on strings 6, 5 and 4 between frets 0 and 12.
Build G major as a C shape (x-10-9-7-8-7).
Which shape plays A major with its root on string 6 at fret 5? (the E shape)
G major is played in two CAGED shapes: which one sat higher on the neck?

lessons.title: The major scale in five positions
lessons.teaches: The major scale can be played in five overlapping positions, one around each CAGED chord shape, which together cover the whole neck.
facts: G major in the E-shape position (second position): string 6 frets 2, 3, 5; string 5 frets 2, 3, 5; string 4 frets 2, 4, 5; string 3 frets 2, 4, 5; string 2 frets 3, 5; string 1 frets 2, 3, 5.
The five positions of G major sit around frets 0 to 4 (G shape), 2 to 5 (E shape), 4 to 8 (D shape), 7 to 10 (C shape) and 9 to 13 (A shape), then repeat twelve frets higher.
Each position overlaps the next, as the chord shapes do, so learning them one at a time links up the whole neck.
Many players also use three-notes-per-string patterns: from G on string 6 fret 3, G major is frets 3 5 7 on strings 6 and 5, 4 5 7 on strings 4 and 3, and 5 7 8 on strings 2 and 1.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: fretboard frets 0 to 15 with the five G major positions outlined in turn and the G roots in the root colour; the E-shape position (frets 2 to 5) in full with finger numbers, the G chord (355433 shape) inside it; tab of that position from the lowest G (string 6 fret 3) up two octaves to string 1 fret 3; audio.

exercises.idea: Play G major in the E-shape position from string 6 fret 3 up two octaves to string 1 fret 3, and back.
In the E-shape position (frets 2 to 5), tap every G (string 6 fret 3, string 4 fret 5, string 1 fret 3).
Which position of G major sits around frets 7 to 10? (the C shape)
Order the G major positions from the nut up: E shape, A shape, G shape, C shape, D shape (G, E, D, C, A).

lessons.title: Chord shapes inside scale positions
lessons.teaches: Each CAGED chord shape sits inside a matching position of the major scale, so the chord shows you the scale's root, third and fifth.
facts: Each CAGED chord shape sits inside a matching position of the major scale.
The notes 1, 3 and 5 inside a scale position form that position's CAGED chord shape.
Knowing the chord shape under your hand tells you where the root, third and fifth are while you play a melody or solo.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: G major scale in the E-shape position (frets 2 to 5) with the G chord tones (355433 shape) in the root, third and fifth colours and the other scale notes plain.

exercises.idea: In the E-shape G major position, tap every B, the third (string 5 fret 2, string 3 fret 4).
Play the G major E-shape scale position, then strum the chord inside it.
The chord tones inside a scale position form a CAGED chord shape (true).

units.checkpoint: The five open shapes; the barre replacing the nut; E-shape and A-shape barre chords (major and minor) with roots on strings 6 and 5; the C-A-G-E-D order up the neck; one chord in five places; the five major-scale positions (and three-notes-per-string patterns); chord shapes inside scale positions.

units.title: The pentatonic in five boxes
units.summary: All five boxes of the minor pentatonic, how they link up the neck, the major pentatonic in the same shapes, and in-tune bends.
units.whyItMatters: Five linked boxes free you from one position, so you can solo anywhere on the neck in any key.

lessons.title: Minor and major pentatonic
lessons.teaches: Minor pentatonic is 1 b3 4 5 b7 and major pentatonic is 1 2 3 5 6, and each minor pentatonic shares its notes with the major pentatonic a minor third above.
facts: Minor pentatonic is 1 b3 4 5 b7: natural minor without degrees 2 and b6.
Major pentatonic is 1 2 3 5 6: the major scale without degrees 4 and 7.
A minor pentatonic has the same notes as C major pentatonic, a minor third above; E minor pentatonic matches G major pentatonic.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: box 1 of A minor pentatonic with each dot labelled by its degree in A minor and, toggled, by its degree in C major.

exercises.idea: Type the notes of E minor pentatonic (E G A B D).
Which major pentatonic has the same notes as D minor pentatonic? (F)
Minor pentatonic formula: 1 _ 4 5 _ (b3, b7).

lessons.title: Box 2
lessons.teaches: Box 2 of the minor pentatonic starts on the scale's second note on string 6 and overlaps the top of box 1.
facts: Box 2 of A minor pentatonic: string 6 frets 8, 10; string 5 frets 7, 10; string 4 frets 7, 10; string 3 frets 7, 9; string 2 frets 8, 10; string 1 frets 8, 10.
Box 2 shares its lower notes with the upper notes of box 1.
Each box starts on string 6 on the next note of the scale: in A, box 1 on A, box 2 on C, box 3 on D, box 4 on E and box 5 on G.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: fretboard frets 4 to 11 with box 1 faded and box 2 bold, the shared notes ringed, the A roots (string 4 fret 7, string 2 fret 10) highlighted; audio.

exercises.idea: Tap every note of box 2 of A minor pentatonic.
Play box 2 up and down.
On which note does box 2 of A minor pentatonic start on string 6? (C)

lessons.title: Box 3
lessons.teaches: Box 3 continues up the neck from box 2, starting on the scale's third note on string 6.
facts: Box 3 of A minor pentatonic: string 6 frets 10, 12; string 5 frets 10, 12; string 4 frets 10, 12; string 3 frets 9, 12; string 2 frets 10, 13; string 1 frets 10, 12.
In box 3 the roots (A) are on string 5 fret 12 and string 2 fret 10.
Box 3 is the widest box: it spans five frets, from fret 9 to fret 13.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: fretboard frets 8 to 14 with box 3 and its roots; audio.

exercises.idea: Tap the two roots in box 3 (string 5 fret 12, string 2 fret 10).
Play box 3 up and down.
A dot on string 3 fret 9 in box 3: name the note (E).

lessons.title: Boxes 4 and 5
lessons.teaches: Boxes 4 and 5 complete the cycle, and in A they also appear low on the neck in open and second position.
facts: Box 4 of A minor pentatonic: string 6 frets 12, 15; string 5 frets 12, 15; strings 4 and 3 frets 12, 14; string 2 frets 13, 15; string 1 frets 12, 15.
Box 5 of A minor pentatonic: string 6 frets 15, 17; string 5 frets 15, 17; strings 4 and 3 frets 14, 17; string 2 frets 15, 17; string 1 frets 15, 17.
Twelve frets lower, box 4 of A minor pentatonic is in open position and box 5 sits around frets 2 to 5.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: boxes 4 and 5 at frets 12 to 17, and the same shapes at frets 0 to 5; audio.

exercises.idea: Tap every note of box 4 of A minor pentatonic in open position.
Play box 5 around frets 2 to 5, up and down.
Which box of A minor pentatonic is in open position? (box 4)

lessons.title: Connecting the boxes
lessons.teaches: The five boxes link end to end, and sliding between them on one string lets a solo travel along the neck.
facts: The five boxes link end to end: the top notes of each box are the bottom notes of the next.
After box 5 comes box 1 again, twelve frets above where it started.
Sliding along one string between boxes connects them smoothly in a solo.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: the full neck with all five A minor pentatonic boxes in alternating shades; tab of an original phrase that slides on string 3 from box 1 (fret 7) to box 2 (fret 9) and on into box 3.

exercises.idea: Play a phrase that starts in box 1 and slides up string 3 into box 2.
Order the boxes of A minor pentatonic from fret 5 upward (1, 2, 3, 4, 5).
Tap the notes box 3 and box 4 share (frets 12 on strings 6, 5, 4, 3 and 1, fret 13 on string 2).

lessons.title: Major pentatonic in the same boxes
lessons.teaches: The major pentatonic uses the same five shapes as its relative minor pentatonic; only the home note changes.
facts: Major pentatonic uses the same five shapes as its relative minor pentatonic; only the root changes.
C major pentatonic uses the same frets as A minor pentatonic, with C as home.
Box 1 of C major pentatonic (root on string 6 fret 8) has exactly the frets of box 2 of A minor pentatonic.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: box 2 of A minor pentatonic redrawn with the C notes as roots; audio of the box over a C drone, then over an A drone.

exercises.idea: Same box over two drones: which one sounds major?
In the C major pentatonic box at fret 8, tap every C.
G major pentatonic uses the boxes of which minor pentatonic? (E)

lessons.title: Bends that land on scale notes
lessons.teaches: A bend should arrive exactly on a scale note, usually a whole step up, and you can check it against the fretted target.
facts: A bend should land in tune on a scale note: a whole step (the pitch of two frets higher) or a half step (one fret).
In box 1 of A minor pentatonic, bending string 3 fret 7 (D) up a whole step reaches E, the 5th.
Bending string 2 fret 8 (G) up a whole step reaches A, the root.
To check a bend, play the target fret first (string 3 fret 9 for E), then bend to match it.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: tab 9 then 7b9 on string 3, and 10 then 8b10 on string 2; audio of each in tune and slightly flat for comparison.

exercises.idea: Bend string 3 fret 7 up a whole step until it matches E4 (string 3 fret 9).
Was the bend in tune, flat or sharp?
Bending the b7 (G) of A minor pentatonic up a whole step lands on which degree? (the root, A)

units.title: The blues
units.summary: The blues scales, the 12-bar form, dominant seventh chords, common variations, and which scale to use over which chord.
units.whyItMatters: The blues is the root of rock, jazz and soul, and the 12-bar form is the first jam every guitarist is expected to know.

lessons.title: The blues scale
lessons.teaches: The minor blues scale is the minor pentatonic with one added note, the flat 5, called the blue note.
facts: The minor blues scale is the minor pentatonic plus the flat 5: 1 b3 4 b5 5 b7.
A blues is A C D Eb E G.
The added b5 is often called the blue note (the b3 and b7 are blue notes too); it is usually passed through on the way to the 4 or the 5 rather than held.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: box 1 of A minor pentatonic with the Eb notes added at string 5 fret 6 and string 3 fret 8; tab of an original lick (a short phrase) sliding string 3 frets 7-8-7 (D Eb D) to string 4 fret 7 (A); audio.

exercises.idea: Tap both blue notes in box 1 of A minor pentatonic (string 5 fret 6, string 3 fret 8).
Type the blue note of E blues (Bb).
Minor pentatonic or blues scale?

lessons.title: The major blues scale
lessons.teaches: The major blues scale is the major pentatonic plus the flat 3, used for a sweeter, country-flavoured blues.
facts: The major blues scale is the major pentatonic plus the flat 3: 1 2 b3 3 5 6.
A major blues is A B C C# E F#.
Moving from the b3 up to the 3 (C to C# in A), by slide or hammer-on, is a classic blues and country sound.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: box 1 of A major pentatonic (root on string 6 fret 5, frets 4 to 7) with the added C notes (string 3 fret 5, string 1 fret 8) in a second colour; tab of a hammer-on from string 3 fret 5 to fret 6 (C to C#); audio.

exercises.idea: A major blues: A B _ C# E F# (C).
Hammer from C to C# on string 3 (frets 5 to 6), then play E on string 2 fret 5.
Which note does major blues add to major pentatonic? (the b3)

lessons.title: The 12-bar form
lessons.teaches: The 12-bar blues is a fixed 12-bar pattern of the I, IV and V chords that repeats for the whole song.
facts: The 12-bar blues is a 12-bar chord pattern built from I, IV and V that repeats for the whole song.
The basic pattern: four bars of I, two of IV, two of I, one of V, one of IV, two of I.
In A the chords are A, D and E; in E they are E, A and B; in G they are G, C and D.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: a 12-bar chart in three lines of four bars (| A | A | A | A | D | D | A | A | E | D | A | A |) with numerals under it and the chord boxes A (x02220), D (xx0232) and E (022100); audio of a backing loop.

exercises.idea: Complete the 12-bar in A: | A | A | A | A | D | D | A | A | _ | D | A | A | (E).
Play through the 12 bars in A with four strums per bar.
Which chord is in bar 10 of the basic 12-bar? (IV)

lessons.title: Dominant seventh chords
lessons.teaches: The blues usually turns all three chords into dominant sevenths, a major triad with a minor seventh added.
facts: A dominant seventh chord is a major triad plus a minor seventh: 1 3 5 b7.
In a blues all three chords are usually dominant sevenths: A7, D7 and E7 in A.
The b7 of I7 and IV7 is outside the major key; the blues breaks the usual key rules on purpose.
Open shapes: A7 x02020, D7 xx0212, E7 020100.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: chord boxes of A7 (x02020), D7 (xx0212) and E7 (020100) with the b7 dot labelled in each; audio of A then A7.

exercises.idea: Hear A, then a second chord: A again or A7?
D7 is D F# A _ (C).

lessons.title: Quick change and turnaround
lessons.teaches: Two common variations change the 12-bar: the quick change (IV in bar 2) and the turnaround (V in bar 12).
facts: The quick change moves to IV in bar 2 and back to I in bar 3.
A turnaround is a passage at the end of a form that leads back to the start; the simplest blues turnaround plays V in bar 12.
With both changes the 12 bars are: I IV I I | IV IV I I | V IV I V.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: the 12-bar chart in E with the quick change and the turnaround highlighted (E7 A7 E7 E7 | A7 A7 E7 E7 | B7 A7 E7 B7); B7 box (x21202); audio.

exercises.idea: Order the chords of bars 9 to 12 with a turnaround in E: B7, A7, E7, B7.
Play the 12 bars in E with the quick change and turnaround.
Where does the quick change go to IV? (bar 2)

lessons.title: Minor or major pentatonic over a blues
lessons.teaches: Over a dominant blues, the tonic's minor pentatonic gives the gritty sound and its major pentatonic the sweet one, and players mix them.
facts: Over a dominant blues in A, A minor pentatonic gives the classic bluesy clash of its C (b3) against the chord's C# (3).
A major pentatonic over the same blues sounds sweeter and more country.
Blues guitarists often mix minor and major pentatonic in the same phrase.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: A minor pentatonic box 1 (fret 5) and A major pentatonic box 1 (root on string 6 fret 5, frets 4 to 7) side by side; audio of each over an A7 backing.

exercises.idea: Over an A7 backing: minor pentatonic or major pentatonic?
Over A7, play a phrase from A minor pentatonic that ends on a C bent a quarter tone, then one from A major pentatonic ending on C#.
Minor pentatonic over a major-key blues sounds wrong and is avoided (false).

lessons.title: The minor blues
lessons.teaches: A minor blues uses the same 12 bars with minor i and iv chords, and the tonic's minor pentatonic or blues scale fits it closely.
facts: A minor blues follows the 12-bar form with minor chords on i and iv.
A minor blues in A uses Am (or Am7), Dm (or Dm7) and E7 (or Em7).
The blues scale of the tonic fits the i and iv chords of a minor blues without the major-minor clash.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: a 12-bar chart in A minor (Am7 x02010, Dm7 xx0211, E7 020100); A blues scale box; audio backing.

exercises.idea: Minor blues in A: bars 5 and 6 are _ (Dm or Dm7).
Is this 12-bar a major (dominant) blues or a minor blues?
Play the minor blues in A once through.

units.title: How chords work: function and cadence
units.summary: Tonic, subdominant and dominant, why V pulls home, the four cadences, common progressions, and how to find a song's key.
units.whyItMatters: Knowing what each chord does lets you predict, remember and write progressions instead of memorising them.

lessons.title: Home, away and tension
lessons.teaches: Chords in a key do one of three jobs: tonic (home), subdominant (moving away) or dominant (tension that wants to return home).
facts: Chords in a key have three functions: tonic (home), subdominant (moving away) and dominant (tension that wants to return).
In a major key, I is the main tonic chord, IV the main subdominant chord and V the main dominant chord.
Many progressions follow the cycle tonic, subdominant, dominant, tonic.
The subdominant function is also called predominant, because it usually comes before the dominant.
Each degree has a name: 1 tonic, 2 supertonic, 3 mediant, 4 subdominant, 5 dominant, 6 submediant, 7 leading tone.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Play C, F, G, C (x32010, xx3211, 320003, x32010) and say "home, away, tension, home". Figure: the three chords with function labels; audio.

exercises.idea: Match each chord in C to its function: C / tonic, F / subdominant, G / dominant.
Does the progression end on the tonic or on the dominant?
Which function wants to resolve home? (dominant)
Match each degree to its name: 1 / tonic, 3 / mediant, 4 / subdominant, 5 / dominant, 7 / leading tone.

lessons.title: Chords that do the same job
lessons.teaches: vi and iii can stand in for I, ii for IV and vii° for V, because they share most of their notes.
facts: vi (and, more weakly, iii) can stand in for the tonic; ii acts as a subdominant chord; vii° acts as a dominant chord.
Chords that share two notes can often replace each other: Dm (D F A) shares F and A with F (F A C).
That is why ii-V-I and IV-V-I do the same job.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: the C major chords grouped in three function columns, tonic C (x32010), Em (022000), Am (x02210); subdominant Dm (xx0231), F (xx3211); dominant G (320003), Bdim (x2343x), with shared notes highlighted; audio of IV-V-I then ii-V-I.

exercises.idea: Which chord can replace IV as a subdominant chord? (ii)
Did you hear IV-V-I or ii-V-I?
vi is a tonic-function chord (true).

lessons.title: Why V pulls home
lessons.teaches: V contains the leading tone (degree 7) and V7 adds degree 4; these two notes form a tritone that resolves by half steps onto the tonic chord.
facts: The V chord contains the leading tone (degree 7), which pulls up a half step to the tonic: B to C in C major.
V7 adds degree 4 (F in G7), which pulls down a half step to degree 3 (E).
The 3rd and 7th of V7 form a tritone (B and F in G7), and its resolution is what makes V7-I so strong.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: G7 (320001) moving to C (x32010): on string 2 the open B rises to C (fret 1) and on string 1 the F (fret 1) falls to the open E; the two moving voices are highlighted; audio played slowly.

exercises.idea: Which note of G7 resolves up to C? (B)
Did the chord resolve or not?
In G7 the tritone is B and _ (F).

lessons.title: Cadences: how phrases end
lessons.teaches: A cadence is the chord move that ends a phrase, and four kinds cover most music: authentic, plagal, half and deceptive.
facts: A cadence is the chord movement that ends a phrase.
Authentic cadence: V (or V7) to I. Plagal cadence: IV to I.
Half cadence: a phrase that ends on V. Deceptive cadence: V to vi.
The authentic cadence sounds the most final; a half cadence sounds like a comma, not a full stop.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: the four cadences in G as chord pairs, D7 (xx0212) to G (320003), C (x32010) to G, Am (x02210) to D (xx0232) and D to Em (022000), with chord boxes; audio of each.

exercises.idea: Match: V-I / authentic, IV-I / plagal, ends on V / half, V-vi / deceptive.
Hear a phrase ending: which cadence?
In C, G to Am is which cadence? (deceptive)

lessons.title: Hearing cadences
lessons.teaches: Each cadence has its own feel, and you can name one by asking: did it end home, and how did it get there?
facts: The deceptive cadence surprises because the ear expects I after V and hears vi, which shares two of I's notes.
The plagal cadence (IV-I) is the "Amen" ending of many hymns.
A phrase ending on V sounds unfinished: it waits for the next phrase.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Audio: short four-chord phrases in C, G and D ending in each cadence, played with open chords such as G7 (320001), C (x32010), Am (x02210), F (xx3211) and D (xx0232). Figure: chord boxes revealed after each answer.

exercises.idea: Authentic or half cadence?
Authentic or deceptive cadence?
Play a plagal cadence in G (C to G).

lessons.title: The progressions everyone uses
lessons.teaches: A handful of progressions built from functions turn up again and again, in every key.
facts: I-IV-V-I moves tonic, subdominant, dominant, tonic.
I-vi-IV-V (in C: C Am F G) is the classic 1950s progression.
ii-V-I (in C: Dm G C) is the central progression of jazz.
vi-IV-I-V is the same loop as I-V-vi-IV, started on a different chord.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Play each progression in G with open chords: G (320003), Em (022000), C (x32010), D (xx0232) and Am (x02210). Figure: numerals over chord boxes; audio loops.

exercises.idea: Which progression: I-vi-IV-V or I-IV-V-I?
ii-V-I in G: _ D G (Am).
Play I-vi-IV-V in G: G, Em, C, D.

lessons.title: Finding the key of a song
lessons.teaches: To find a song's key, list its chords, see which major key contains them, and listen for the chord that feels like home.
facts: The key's tonic chord is the chord the song feels at rest on, often the first and last chord.
If all the chords fit one major key, look for its I, IV and V: G, C, D and Em point to G major.
The same chords fit a major key and its relative minor; the chord that sounds like home decides which.

The loop Am F C G: does it feel at home on Am or on C?
The first chord of a song is always its key (false).

units.title: Reading music: the whole first position
units.summary: All six strings in first position, accidentals within a bar, rhythm on the staff, repeats and road signs, dynamics and articulation.
units.whyItMatters: With first position, accidentals and the road map you can read most beginner and folk guitar music at sight.

lessons.title: Reading on strings 4 to 6
lessons.teaches: In first position the naturals on strings 4 to 6 are D, E, F; A, B, C; and E, F, G, written on and below the bottom of the staff.
facts: First-position naturals: string 4 D (open), E (2), F (3); string 5 A (open), B (2), C (3); string 6 E (open), F (1), G (3).
The written E on the bottom line is string 4 fret 2; the F in the bottom space is string 4 fret 3.
The written F on the third ledger line below the staff is string 6 fret 1; the G just above that line is string 6 fret 3.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: staff from written E3 to F4 above a fretboard of strings 6 to 4, frets 0 to 3, each note joined to its fret; an original eight-bar melody on these strings; audio.

exercises.idea: Name the written note on the first ledger line below the staff (C).
Place the written note for string 6 fret 3 (G, in the space above the third ledger line).
Read and play an eight-bar melody on strings 4 to 6.
Tap where the written C on the first ledger line below the staff is played in first position (string 5, fret 3).

lessons.title: Accidentals last until the bar line
lessons.teaches: An accidental in the music lasts to the end of its bar on that line or space, and a natural sign cancels it.
facts: An accidental written before a note lasts until the end of that bar.
It applies to notes on the same line or space only, not to the same letter in another octave.
A natural sign cancels a sharp or flat; the bar line cancels accidentals too, except that a note tied across the bar line keeps its accidental.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: two bars on the staff: an F# then two more Fs on the same space (both F#), a natural sign, then the next bar starting on F natural; fretboard showing string 4 frets 3 and 4.

exercises.idea: In a bar that began with F#, name the next F on the same space with no sign (F#).
An accidental lasts for the rest of the piece (false).
Which sign cancels a sharp: a flat or a natural sign? (a natural sign)

lessons.title: Sharps and flats in first position
lessons.teaches: In first position a sharp is one fret above its natural and a flat one fret below, and a flat below an open string moves to the next thicker string.
facts: In first position a sharp is played one fret above its natural and a flat one fret below, on the same string where possible.
A flat on an open-string note is played on the next thicker string: Bb3 at string 3 fret 3, Eb4 at string 2 fret 4.
F# on string 1 is fret 2 and C# on string 2 is fret 2.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: staff with written F#5, C#5, Bb4 and Eb5 (sounding F#4, C#4, Bb3, Eb4), each joined to its first-position fret.

exercises.idea: Name the written note on the top line with a sharp before it (F#; it is played at string 1 fret 2).
Tap where Bb3 is played in first position (string 3, fret 3).
Place written Eb in the top space (E with a flat).

lessons.title: Stems, beams and reading rhythm
lessons.teaches: Stems and beams show rhythm on the staff, and beams group notes by the beat so you can see where each beat starts.
facts: Notes below the middle line usually have stems going up on the right; notes above it have stems going down on the left.
Beams group eighth and sixteenth notes by the beat, so each beat's start is easy to see.
To read a new piece, tap its rhythm first, then find the notes, then put the two together.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: two bars on the staff mixing quarters, beamed eighths and a dotted quarter, with notes on strings 1 to 3 in first position (frets 0 to 3) and the counts under them; audio.

exercises.idea: Tap the rhythm of the two bars shown before playing them.

Play the two bars on strings 1 to 3 in first position.

lessons.title: Repeats and road signs
lessons.teaches: Repeat signs, endings, D.C., D.S., Fine and coda tell you the order in which to play the sections of a piece.
facts: Repeat signs (thick and thin bar lines with two dots) mean play the passage between them again.
With first and second endings, play the first ending the first time and skip to the second ending on the repeat.
D.C. (da capo) means go back to the beginning; D.S. (dal segno) means go back to the sign, a slanted S with two dots.
"al Fine" means stop at the word Fine; "al Coda" means jump to the coda (marked with a circle and cross) when you reach "To Coda".
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: an original 16-bar lead sheet in G with chord boxes (G 320003, C x32010, D xx0232), repeat signs, first and second endings, D.S. al Coda and a coda, with the playing order animated bar by bar.

exercises.idea: Section A has repeat signs with first and second endings, then B follows. Put in playing order: B, A with the second ending, A with the first ending (A with the first ending, A with the second ending, B).
What does D.C. al Fine mean? (go back to the start and stop at Fine)

Match: D.C. / from the beginning, D.S. / from the sign, Fine / the end, Coda / the closing section.

lessons.title: Dynamics and articulation
lessons.teaches: Letters and signs on the staff tell you how loud to play and how each note should start and end.
facts: Dynamics from soft to loud: pp, p, mp, mf, f, ff (pianissimo, piano, mezzo-piano, mezzo-forte, forte, fortissimo).
A crescendo (cresc. or an opening wedge) means gradually louder; a diminuendo (dim. or a closing wedge) means gradually softer.
A dot above or below a note (staccato) means short and detached; a short line (tenuto) means hold it its full length.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: an original four-bar phrase on strings 1 and 2 (frets 0 to 3) on the staff, marked p, crescendo, f, with staccato notes (cut each one short by easing the fretting finger off, or by touching an open string) and tenuto notes; audio played as marked.

exercises.idea: Order from softest to loudest: f, p, mf, pp, ff, mp.

Match: p / soft, f / loud, cresc. / getting louder, staccato / short.

units.title: Harmony in minor keys
units.summary: The chords of a minor key, the borrowed major V, common minor progressions, the Andalusian cadence and other minor-key colours.
units.whyItMatters: Most rock, metal, flamenco and many pop songs live in minor keys, and their chords follow these patterns.

lessons.title: The chords of a minor key
lessons.teaches: Stacking thirds in natural minor gives minor, diminished, major, minor, minor, major, major chords.
facts: The natural-minor triads are, from degree 1 to 7: minor, diminished, major, minor, minor, major, major.
In A minor the chords are Am, Bdim, C, Dm, Em, F and G.
This app writes them i ii° bIII iv v bVI bVII, measuring each root against the major scale; many classical books write III, VI and VII instead.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: chord boxes of the A minor chords (Am x02210, Bdim on strings 4-3-2, C x32010, Dm xx0231, Em 022000, F small barre xx3211, G 320003) with numerals; audio.

exercises.idea: The chords of E minor: Em, F#dim, G, Am, Bm, _, D (C).
In A minor, which chord is bVI? (F)
In natural minor the chord on degree 5 is major (false).

lessons.title: The borrowed major V
lessons.teaches: Raising the 7th of the minor scale turns v into a major V (and vii into vii°), giving minor keys a strong V-i cadence.
facts: Using the raised 7th of harmonic minor makes the chord on degree 5 major: V (E or E7 in A minor).
The major V contains the leading tone (G# in A minor), which pulls up to the tonic and makes V-i a strong cadence.
The raised 7th also gives a diminished chord on degree 7: vii° (G#dim in A minor).
lessons.onTheGuitar: Play Am, Dm, Em, Am, then Am, Dm, E, Am (E 022100 has G# on string 3). Figure: Em and E boxes with the G/G# note labelled; audio of both endings.

exercises.idea: Did the minor-key phrase end with v-i or V-i?
What is the major V chord in D minor? (A or A7)
Type the leading tone of E minor (D#).

lessons.title: Common minor progressions
lessons.teaches: A few progressions built from i, iv, v, bVI, bVII and bIII make up much of minor-key rock and pop.
facts: i-bVII-bVI-bVII (Am G F G) and i-bVI-bIII-bVII (Am F C G) are common minor-key loops in rock and pop.
i-iv-v and i-iv-V are the basic minor-key progressions.
Ending bVII-i (G to Am) is a common rock cadence; its bVII is built on the subtonic, the note a whole step below the tonic, so there is no leading tone.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Play each loop in A minor (Am x02210, G 320003, F xx3211, C x32010) and in E minor (Em 022000, D xx0232, C, G). Figure: numerals over chord boxes; audio.

exercises.idea: Which loop: i-bVII-bVI-bVII or i-bVI-bIII-bVII?

Play Am, G, F, G.

lessons.title: The Andalusian cadence
lessons.teaches: The Andalusian cadence is the descending minor progression i-bVII-bVI-V.
facts: The Andalusian cadence is i-bVII-bVI-V: in A minor, Am G F E.
Its bass walks down a step at a time from the tonic to the fifth: A G F E.
It is central to flamenco and also turns up in many rock and pop songs.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Play Am (x02210), G (320003), F (xx3211 or 133211), E (022100) over a steady strum. Figure: chord boxes with the bass line marked; audio.

exercises.idea: Order the Andalusian cadence in A minor: E, Am, F, G (Am, G, F, E).
Is this the Andalusian cadence?
Type the last chord of the Andalusian cadence in D minor (A).

lessons.title: Moving between relative keys
lessons.teaches: Because relative keys share their chords, songs often shift between a major key and its relative minor without any new chords.
facts: Relative keys share all their diatonic chords, so a song can move between them without any new chords.
A verse can rest on vi (Am in C) and a chorus on I (C), changing the home feeling without changing key signature.
The major V of the relative minor (E or E7 in C major) is the chord that most clearly pulls toward the minor.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: a two-part original chart in C with open chords (Am x02210, F xx3211, C x32010, G 320003, E7 020100): verse Am F C G (resting on Am), chorus C G Am F (resting on C), with an E7 before the return to Am; audio.

exercises.idea: Does this section feel at home on Am or on C?
Which chord pulls a C major song toward A minor? (E or E7)
Moving to the relative minor requires a new key signature (false).

lessons.title: The Picardy third and the major IV
lessons.teaches: Two bright colours in minor: ending on a major tonic chord (the Picardy third) and a major IV chord made with the raised 6th of melodic minor.
facts: Ending a minor-key piece on a major tonic chord is called a Picardy third.
A major IV in a minor key (D in A minor) gives a brighter minor sound.
That major IV uses the raised 6th of melodic minor (F# in A minor) in place of the natural minor's F.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Play Am (x02210), D (xx0232), Am, D, and an ending Dm, E, A. Figure: chord boxes with the F#/F and C#/C differences labelled; audio.

exercises.idea: Did the minor piece end on a minor or a major tonic chord?
In A minor, which note makes the IV chord major? (F#)
A Picardy third is a major chord at the end of a minor-key piece (true).

units.title: Seventh chords
units.summary: The five main seventh chords, their formulas, the sevenths of major and minor keys, open and barre shapes, and what each one does.
units.whyItMatters: Seventh chords are the sound of jazz, soul, funk and the blues, and they explain how chords pull from one to the next.

lessons.title: Adding a seventh
lessons.teaches: A seventh chord is a triad with one more third stacked on top, giving root, third, fifth and seventh.
facts: A seventh chord is a triad with another third stacked on top: root, 3rd, 5th and 7th.
Its type depends on the triad and on the size of the seventh: a major 7th is eleven half steps above the root, a minor 7th ten.
The five main types are major 7 (maj7), dominant 7 (7), minor 7 (m7), half-diminished (m7b5) and diminished 7 (dim7).
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: C (x32010) and Cmaj7 (x32000) side by side, with the B on open string 2 labelled 7; audio.

exercises.idea: How many half steps above the root is a major 7th? (11)
Triad or seventh chord?
Turn C into Cmaj7 by lifting one finger (x32000).

lessons.title: Five seventh-chord formulas
lessons.teaches: maj7, 7, m7, m7b5 and dim7 each have their own formula of thirds.
facts: m7b5 (half-diminished, ø7) = 1 b3 b5 b7; dim7 (°7) = 1 b3 b5 bb7.
The 7th of a diminished seventh is a double flat: Cdim7 is C Eb Gb Bbb, and Bbb sounds like A.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: the five C seventh chords spelled out on a keyboard and as dots on strings 5 to 2 from C at string 5 fret 3; audio.

lessons.title: The seventh chords of a major key
lessons.teaches: Stacking four notes on each degree of a major key gives Imaj7 ii7 iii7 IVmaj7 V7 vi7 viiø7.
facts: The diatonic seventh chords of a major key are Imaj7 ii7 iii7 IVmaj7 V7 vi7 viiø7.
In C major they are Cmaj7, Dm7, Em7, Fmaj7, G7, Am7 and Bm7b5.
Only one diatonic chord in a major key is a dominant seventh: V7.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: the seven chords of C as four-note shapes on strings 5 to 2, numerals underneath; audio climbing through them.

exercises.idea: The seventh chords of G: Gmaj7, Am7, Bm7, Cmaj7, _, Em7, F#m7b5 (D7).
Which degree of a major key has a half-diminished chord? (7)
In F major, which chord is IVmaj7? (Bbmaj7)

lessons.title: The seventh chords of a minor key
lessons.teaches: Stacking four notes on each degree of natural minor gives i7 iiø7 bIIImaj7 iv7 v7 bVImaj7 bVII7, and the raised 7th of harmonic minor adds the dominant V7 and the diminished vii°7.
facts: In A minor the natural-minor seventh chords are Am7, Bm7b5, Cmaj7, Dm7, Em7, Fmaj7 and G7.
This app writes them i7 iiø7 bIIImaj7 iv7 v7 bVImaj7 bVII7.
With the raised 7th of harmonic minor (G# in A minor), v7 becomes the dominant seventh E7 and the chord on G# becomes the diminished seventh G#dim7.
On the tonic the raised 7th gives a minor-major seventh chord, AmMaj7 (A C E G#): a minor triad with a major 7th.

lessons.title: Open seventh-chord shapes
lessons.teaches: Many open chords become seventh chords by moving or lifting one finger.
facts: Open maj7 shapes: Cmaj7 x32000 and Fmaj7 xx3210.
Open m7 shapes: Am7 x02010, Em7 022030 and Dm7 xx0211.
Open dominant 7 shapes: G7 320001, C7 x32310 and B7 x21202.

lessons.title: Movable seventh-chord shapes
lessons.teaches: The E-shape and A-shape barre chords have seventh versions you can move to any root on strings 6 and 5.
facts: E-shape sevenths with the root on string 6 (at fret 1, F): F7 131211, Fm7 131111, Fmaj7 1x221x.
A-shape sevenths with the root on string 5 (at fret 1, Bb): Bb7 x13131, Bbm7 x13121, Bbmaj7 x13231.
A common half-diminished shape with the root on string 5 is x1212x (Bbm7b5 at fret 1).

lessons.title: Hearing seventh chords
lessons.teaches: Each seventh chord has a recognisable colour, and the top note's distance from the octave tells major 7th from minor 7th.
facts: maj7 is often described as soft and dreamy, 7 as bluesy and restless, m7 as mellow, m7b5 as dark and unstable, dim7 as tense.
A major 7th is a half step below the octave and rubs against it; a minor 7th is a whole step below.
To tell 7 from m7, listen for the third: major in 7, minor in m7.

lessons.title: What each seventh chord does
lessons.teaches: maj7 chords rest, dominant 7 chords pull, m7 chords prepare, and the diminished family leads to the next chord.
facts: maj7 chords usually act as tonic (Imaj7) or subdominant (IVmaj7) chords.
Dominant 7 chords want to resolve, most often down a fifth: G7 to C.
m7b5 chords act as ii in minor keys or vii in major keys; dim7 chords act as leading-tone (vii°7) dominant chords.

units.title: The modes
units.summary: The seven modes of the major scale as scales and as colours, their characteristic notes and vamps, and how to hear them.
units.whyItMatters: Modes give you seven distinct moods from one set of notes, and explain the sound of a lot of rock, folk, funk and film music.

lessons.title: Same notes, new home
lessons.teaches: A mode is the scale you get by starting a scale on a different note and treating that note as home.
facts: A mode is a scale made by starting a scale on a different note and treating that note as home.
The seven modes of the major scale, starting on degrees 1 to 7, are Ionian, Dorian, Phrygian, Lydian, Mixolydian, Aeolian and Locrian.
The natural notes from D to D make D Dorian; from G to G, G Mixolydian.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: the C major notes along string 5 with the start moving from C to D to E, each labelled with its mode name; audio of C Ionian and D Dorian over their own drones.

exercises.idea: Put the modes in order from degree 1: Lydian, Ionian, Phrygian, Dorian (Ionian, Dorian, Phrygian, Lydian).

The natural notes from E to E make which mode? (E Phrygian)

lessons.title: Comparing each mode with major
lessons.teaches: Comparing each mode with the major scale on the same tonic shows its colour, and the modes line up from brightest to darkest.
facts: Against the major scale on the same tonic: Lydian has #4; Mixolydian b7; Dorian b3 b7; Aeolian b3 b6 b7; Phrygian b2 b3 b6 b7; Locrian b2 b3 b5 b6 b7.
Ionian is the major scale and Aeolian is the natural minor.
From brightest to darkest: Lydian, Ionian, Mixolydian, Dorian, Aeolian, Phrygian, Locrian.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: seven one-octave shapes from A on string 6 fret 5, one per mode, with the altered degrees highlighted; audio of each over an A drone.

exercises.idea: Match each mode to its difference from major: Lydian / #4, Mixolydian / b7, Dorian / b3 b7, Phrygian / b2 b3 b6 b7.
Order from brightest to darkest: Dorian, Lydian, Phrygian, Mixolydian (Lydian, Mixolydian, Dorian, Phrygian).
Type the notes of A Mixolydian (A B C# D E F# G).

lessons.title: Dorian
lessons.teaches: Dorian is natural minor with a raised 6th, a minor sound with a brighter edge; it is the F# of the major IV in A minor heard as a scale.
facts: Dorian is 1 2 b3 4 5 6 b7: natural minor with a raised 6th.
The raised 6th is Dorian's characteristic note: B in D Dorian, F# in A Dorian.
Dorian suits a vamp (two chords repeated over and over) of the minor tonic and the major IV: Dm to G, or Am to D.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Vamp Am7 (x02010) to D (xx0232) and play A Dorian in fifth position: A natural minor with F# (string 4 fret 4, string 2 fret 7) in place of F. Figure: A Dorian in fifth position with F# highlighted; audio.

lessons.title: Mixolydian
lessons.teaches: Mixolydian is the major scale with a flat 7th, the sound of the dominant seventh chord.
facts: Mixolydian is 1 2 3 4 5 6 b7: the major scale with a flat 7th.
Its b7 matches the dominant seventh chord, so G Mixolydian fits G7.
Mixolydian suits major vamps with a bVII chord: G to F, or A to G.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Vamp A (x02220) to G (320003) and play A Mixolydian; figure: A Mixolydian around fret 5 with G highlighted; audio.

exercises.idea: Type the b7 of D Mixolydian (C).

lessons.title: Lydian
lessons.teaches: Lydian is the major scale with a raised 4th, a bright, floating major sound.
facts: Lydian is 1 2 3 #4 5 6 7: the major scale with a raised 4th.
The #4 is Lydian's characteristic note: B in F Lydian, C# in G Lydian.
Lydian suits a vamp from the I chord to a major chord a whole step up: F to G in F Lydian.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Vamp D (xx0232) to E (022100) and play D Lydian (with G#); figure: D Lydian one-octave shape from string 5 fret 5 with G# highlighted; audio.

exercises.idea: Type the #4 of C Lydian (F#).

lessons.title: Phrygian and Locrian
lessons.teaches: Phrygian is natural minor with a flat 2nd, and Locrian adds a flat 5th, which makes its tonic chord diminished.
facts: Phrygian is 1 b2 b3 4 5 b6 b7: natural minor with a flat 2nd, a dark, Spanish-sounding colour.
Phrygian's signature move is the major chord a half step above the tonic, bII, falling to i: F to Em in E Phrygian.
Locrian is 1 b2 b3 4 b5 b6 b7; its tonic chord is diminished, so it rarely works as a home key, but it fits m7b5 chords.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Play F (133211) to Em (022000) and E Phrygian in open position (E F G A B C D on strings 6 to 1); figure: open E Phrygian with F highlighted; audio.

exercises.idea: Type the b2 of A Phrygian (Bb).
Phrygian or Aeolian?
The tonic chord of Locrian is diminished (true).

lessons.title: Hearing the modes
lessons.teaches: A mode only sounds like itself when its tonic feels like home, so practise and hear modes over a drone or a vamp, thinking of the parent scale's notes.
facts: A mode is heard as that mode only when its tonic sounds like home, usually through a drone or a repeating vamp.
Over an A drone, A Dorian (with F#) sounds minor but brighter, A Phrygian (with Bb) darker, A Mixolydian (with C# and G) major but bluesy.
To play a mode, take the notes of its parent major scale and centre everything on the mode's tonic: A Dorian uses the notes of G major.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Audio: a sustained A drone (open string 5) under each mode played from A2. Figure: each mode's altered notes on the neck appear after the answer.

exercises.idea: Over an A drone: name the mode (Ionian, Dorian, Phrygian, Lydian, Mixolydian, Aeolian).
Which major scale is the parent of E Mixolydian? (A major)
Over an open-string-5 drone, play A Mixolydian and end on A.

units.checkpoint: Modes as rotations of the major scale and their names in order; each mode's formula against the major scale and the bright-to-dark order; the characteristic note and typical vamp of Dorian, Mixolydian, Lydian and Phrygian; why Locrian is rarely a home key; naming a mode's parent major scale; hearing modes over a drone.

units.title: Colour chords: sus, add, 6 and slash
units.summary: Suspended, added-note and sixth chords, slash chords, bass lines and pedal points.
units.whyItMatters: These small changes to familiar shapes are where much of the shimmer in acoustic and pop guitar comes from.

lessons.title: Suspended chords
lessons.teaches: A suspended chord replaces the 3rd with the 2nd or the 4th, so it is neither major nor minor.
facts: A suspended chord replaces the 3rd with the 2nd (sus2) or the 4th (sus4): Csus2 is C D G, Csus4 is C F G.
With no 3rd, a sus chord is neither major nor minor.
A sus4 often resolves to the major chord on the same root: Dsus4 (xx0233) to D (xx0232).
A 7sus4 chord adds the b7 to a sus4: A7sus4 (x02030) is A D E G, often used in place of V7 or just before it.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: chord boxes of Dsus2 (xx0230), D (xx0232), Dsus4 (xx0233) and Asus2 (x02200), A, Asus4 (x02230), with the moving note labelled 2, 3 or 4; audio.

exercises.idea: Place Asus4 (x02230).
Does the chord sound suspended or resolved?
Gsus4 is G _ D (C).

lessons.title: Added-note chords
lessons.teaches: An add chord keeps the triad and adds one note, such as the 9th, without a 7th.
facts: An add9 chord is a triad plus the 9th, with no 7th: Cadd9 is C E G D.
C9 also has the b7: C E G Bb D.
add4 keeps the 3rd and adds the 4th (Cadd4 is C E F G); add11 adds the same note an octave higher.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: chord boxes of C (x32010), Cadd9 (x32030) and C9 (x32333); audio.

exercises.idea: Place Cadd9 (x32030).
Which chord has a 7th: Cadd9 or C9? (C9)
Type the added note of Gadd9 (A).

lessons.title: Sixth chords
lessons.teaches: A 6 chord adds the major 6th to a triad, and C6 has the same notes as Am7.
facts: A 6 chord is a major triad plus the major 6th: C6 is C E G A.
A minor 6 chord adds the major 6th to a minor triad: Am6 is A C E F#.
C6 and Am7 contain the same four notes; the bass note decides which name fits.
A 6/9 chord adds both the 6th and the 9th to a major triad: C6/9 (x32233) is C E G A D.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: chord boxes of C6 (x35555) and Am7 (x02010) with the shared notes C, E, G and A highlighted, and Am6 (x02212); audio.

exercises.idea: G6 is G B D _ (E).
Which chord has the same notes as C6? (Am7)
Major triad or 6 chord?

lessons.title: Slash chords
lessons.teaches: A slash chord names a chord and a bass note; the bass is either a chord tone (an inversion) or a new note that adds colour.
facts: A slash chord names a chord and its bass note, written chord/bass: D/F#.
If the bass is a chord tone, the slash chord is an inversion: D/F# is D in first inversion.
If the bass is not a chord tone, it adds a new colour: D/C puts C under D, the same notes as D7 with C in the bass.
lessons.onTheGuitar: Figure: chord boxes of D/F# (2x0232, thumb or finger 1 on string 6 fret 2), G/B (x20003) and D/C (x30232); audio.

exercises.idea: Place G/B (x20003).
Is D/F# an inversion? (yes, first inversion)
